hooks.hook: You’ve had filter coffee. Now meet its 1970s ancestor in Koramangala.
Why do Bangaloreites start their day with this?
Filter coffee is how Bangalore wakes up.
This isn’t just coffee—it’s the city’s morning rhythm.

chosen_hook.hook: Filter coffee is how Bangalore wakes up.
chosen_hook.reason: It creates a vivid, relatable image of filter coffee as a daily ritual that encapsulates Bangalore’s culture in a way that feels authentic and specific to the audience.

storyboard.title: Why Bangalore Loves Filter Coffee
storyboard.hook: Filter coffee is how Bangalore wakes up.

shots.visual_prompt: Frothy South Indian filter coffee in a small stainless steel tumbler sitting inside a steel davara bowl, on a worn wooden table in a Bangalore kitchen, early morning window light, steam rising.
shots.overlay_text: Filter coffee is how Bangalore wakes up.
shots.vo_line: Filter coffee is how Bangalore wakes up.

shots.visual_prompt: A man in a checked shirt standing at the steel counter of a busy Bangalore darshini eatery at 7 in the morning, holding a small steel tumbler of frothy filter coffee, other customers blurred behind, soft morning light.
shots.vo_line: It is the first order at every Darshini.

shots.visual_prompt: Close-up of hands pouring frothy filter coffee in a long stream from a steel tumbler held high into a steel davara bowl below, coffee stall counter behind, warm morning light.
shots.vo_line: Poured high, from tumbler to davara.

shots.visual_prompt: A small roadside coffee stall beside a carved stone South Indian temple gateway, a vendor in a white dhoti handing a steel tumbler of coffee to a customer, golden early morning light.
shots.vo_line: Outside temples, on street corners, after the commute.

shots.visual_prompt: Close-up of hot milk being poured from a small steel pot into a stainless steel tumbler of dark coffee, on a granite kitchen counter, steam rising, warm morning light.
shots.vo_line: Strong decoction, hot milk, sugar. Nothing else.
